title: Extend depth sweep: DEPTH=10 -> 12
description: Set DEPTH=12 (from 10); OOM'd at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 so reduced to 64 (grad_accum 2->4, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE unchanged) to fit in 79GB VRAM.
reflection: Clear regression: val_bpb 1.015935, worse than both the depth=10 baseline (1.002279) and the original starting baseline (1.014027). The depth increase itself may still be beneficial, but this result is confounded by the forced DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE cut from 128->64, which quadruples grad_accum_steps and changes optimization dynamics (smaller per-microbatch statistics, more Muon/AdamW steps' worth of noise per optimizer step) independent of depth. Peak VRAM ended up only 49GB, well under budget, suggesting batch size could have stayed higher with more careful accounting -- the depth=10 run's 66.5GB reported figure apparently included some slack I misjudged. Recommendation: do not conclude depth=12 is worse than depth=10 from this alone. If depth is revisited, the correct next experiment is DEPTH=12 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE kept at 128 or 96 (adjusting something else, e.g. gradient checkpointing or n_kv_head<n_head, to control memory) so depth is the only isolated variable. Given budget pressure, I'd deprioritize further depth-only sweeps at 12 unless someone has a clean way to keep batch size fixed.
